name: user_roles
description: Roles held by a user. One role per row.

columns.name: role
columns.description: Stored as a string. An unrecognised value is ignored with a warning, never rejected — see types/RoleNames.json.

columns.name: visible_creation_groups
columns.description: A moderator's visibility scope: JSON array of creation-group strings plus the sentinels '*all' and '*untagged'. NULL means no restriction.

notes: JSON inside a text column: both implementations must parse it the same way, including what an invalid document does. Currently unspecified — write the answer here before either implementation reads the column.
gradido2 adds roles and role_rights tables on top of this (see Architecture.md, Auth). Those are not yet contracted.
created_at and updated_at are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json.

Identifiers are uint64 throughout. Legacy is inconsistent here — users.id is int unsigned while referrer_id, contribution_link_id and publisher_id, which point at it, are bigint unsigned. A foreign key narrower than its target truncates silently in C, so gradido2 uses one width everywhere.
